prompt: Research one embodied-AI and humanoid component-supply-chain investment idea.

inputs.seed_claim: Humanoids, broader robotics, and drones may increase demand for precision motion, sensors, edge compute, batteries, copper wiring, and rare-earth magnets, but paid multi-site economics and supplier materiality remain unproven.
inputs.drivers: Physical-AI progress; labour scarcity; automation; defence and civil drones; falling component costs; trusted supply chains; material constraints; safety, uptime, maintenance, and fixed-automation competition.
inputs.value_chain: Actuators, motors, reducers, bearings, sensors, connectors, edge AI, power semiconductors, batteries, copper, NdPr magnets, integrators, and automation substitutes.
inputs.supporting_evidence: The seed requires pilots to become repeat orders and qualified component suppliers to show recurring material revenue and pricing power.
inputs.invalidation: Humanoids remain pilots, drones commoditise, Asia retains sourcing, per-unit material intensity falls, and supplier margins fade despite unit growth.
